predecessors.name: Province of Quebec
predecessors.text: southern Ontario, the north shore of Lakes Ontario and Erie: the Upper Canada of 1791, west of the Ottawa River

successors.name: Province of Canada
successors.text: southern Ontario, the north shore of Lakes Ontario and Erie: the Upper Canada of 1791, west of the Ottawa River

ledger.x: 1813: the Americans take the Niagara peninsula.
1813: the Americans leave the Niagara peninsula.
1815: Mackinac and Fort Niagara are handed back.
1815: the war ends on ratification, 17 February 1815.
1841: Upper Canada is united with Lower Canada.
1841: the colony is dissolved on 10 February 1841; its territory becomes Canada West.

wars.name: War of 1812
wars.outcome: Britain held Mackinac and Detroit from 1812 (Detroit to September 1813), the Americans occupied the Niagara peninsula May-December 1813 and the British took Fort Niagara in December 1813; 'The Treaty of Ghent restored the pre-war territorial status quo'…

wars.name: Upper Canada Rebellion
wars.outcome: An insurrection 'against the oligarchic government of the Family Compact in December 1837'; 'resistance lingered until 1838 (and became more violent)'; no territory changed hands.

certainty.note: The 1791 act 'did not yet specify official borders'; the boundary with the United States was unsettled.

'The 1795 Jay Treaty officially set the borders between British North America and the United States' (Upper Canada page): the southern border through the lakes is sharp; the northern and western limits of the colony stay soft.
